title: Efficient and Long-Tailed Generalization for Pre-trained Vision-Language Model

problem.claim: Adapting CLIP to downstream tasks may involve long-tailed class distributions, limited samples for some classes, and emerging classes with no samples.

gap.claim: Existing adaptation must address both class imbalance and generalization to new classes without training images while remaining efficient.

contributions.claim: Candle is a framework for efficient and long-tailed generalization of pre-trained vision-language models.
The framework combines compensating logit-adjusted loss, black-box feature-based visual and textual prototypes, cross-modal attention, and virtual prototypes for new classes.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly present Candle as a novel framework for efficient and long-tailed generalization.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report state-of-the-art performance across extensive experiments on 11 diverse datasets.
The authors report substantially reduced training time.
Source code is reported as available in a public GitHub repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Pre-trained vision-language models provide strong zero-shot inference and few-shot learning capabilities.
Downstream adaptation faces long-tailed distributions, limited class samples, and unseen classes without samples.
Candle addresses these challenges through imbalance-aware loss, prototype-based efficient adaptation, cross-modal attention, and virtual prototypes.
The authors report strong performance on 11 datasets and reduced training time.

source_observation.claim: The method uses virtual prototypes to represent new classes lacking training images.

interpretation.claim: Prototype-based representations can support generalization when direct examples for a class are unavailable.

application.claim: Consider combining semantic or multimodal prototypes with adaptation methods for evolving label spaces.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish how virtual prototypes are constructed or when they fail.

source_observation.claim: The framework treats CLIP as a black box and adapts using extracted features.

interpretation.claim: Feature-level adaptation may reduce training requirements while preserving access to pretrained multimodal representations.

application.claim: For efficient downstream adaptation, evaluate whether frozen-model features and lightweight prototype mechanisms are sufficient.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the computational savings, adaptation constraints, or feature quality limits.

unknowns: The abstract does not provide dataset names, metrics, baselines, or numerical results.
The abstract does not describe the training procedure, hyperparameters, ablations, or computational details.
The abstract does not establish independent verification of the reported state-of-the-art performance or training-time reduction.
